main.name: Ajahn Brahm
main.schoolLabel: Thai Forest · Ajahn Chah line (Bodhinyana / BSWA)
main.bio: English-born monk of the Ajahn Chah line, abbot of Bodhinyana Monastery in Western Australia and spiritual director of the BSWA; known for humorous, story-driven talks on meditation, letting go and jhāna.

main.name: Ajahn Brahmali
main.schoolLabel: Thai Forest · Ajahn Chah line (Bodhinyana / BSWA)
main.bio: Norwegian-born monk trained under Ajahn Brahm at Bodhinyana; teaches the early suttas and Vinaya closely, often co-teaching sutta courses with Bhante Sujato.

main.name: Bhante Sujato
main.schoolLabel: Early-Buddhism scholar-monk (Santi / SuttaCentral; trained in the Chah line)
main.bio: Australian monk ordained in the Ajahn Chah tradition; founder of Santi Forest Monastery and co-founder of SuttaCentral, where he has published free English translations of the four main Nikāyas.

main.name: Ajahn Hasapanna
main.schoolLabel: Thai Forest · Ajahn Chah line (Bodhinyana / BSWA)
main.bio: Monk of the Bodhinyana / BSWA community in Western Australia, a student of Ajahn Brahm.

main.name: Ajahn Sumedho
main.schoolLabel: Thai Forest · Ajahn Chah line (Amaravati / Chithurst)
main.bio: American monk, one of Ajahn Chah's first Western disciples; founded Chithurst (Cittaviveka) and Amaravati monasteries in England and led the Forest Sangha in the West for decades.

main.name: Ajahn Amaro
main.schoolLabel: Thai Forest · Ajahn Chah line (Amaravati / Abhayagiri)
main.bio: English monk of the Ajahn Chah line; co-founded Abhayagiri in California and later became abbot of Amaravati.

main.name: Ajahn Pasanno
main.schoolLabel: Thai Forest · Ajahn Chah line (Abhayagiri / Wat Pah Nanachat)
main.bio: Canadian monk ordained under Ajahn Chah; former abbot of Wat Pah Nanachat and long-time co-abbot then abbot of Abhayagiri Buddhist Monastery.

main.name: Ajahn Ñāṇiko
main.bio: Senior monk at Abhayagiri Buddhist Monastery in the Ajahn Chah tradition; gives many of the monastery's evening and retreat talks.

main.name: Ajahn Karuṇadhammo
main.bio: American monk of the Ajahn Chah tradition and former abbot of Abhayagiri.

main.name: Ajahn Cunda
main.bio: Monk of Abhayagiri Buddhist Monastery in the Ajahn Chah tradition.

main.name: Ajahn Sudhīro
main.bio: Monk of Abhayagiri Buddhist Monastery in the Ajahn Chah tradition.

main.name: Ajahn Sucitto
main.schoolLabel: Thai Forest · Ajahn Chah line (Cittaviveka / Chithurst)
main.bio: English monk who trained in Thailand and with Ajahn Sumedho; long-time abbot of Cittaviveka (Chithurst) and author of books on the path and on embodied meditation.

main.name: Ajahn Ahiṃsako
main.schoolLabel: Thai Forest · Ajahn Chah line (Cittaviveka / Chithurst)
main.bio: Monk of Cittaviveka (Chithurst) Buddhist Monastery in the Ajahn Chah tradition.

main.name: Ajahn Karuniko
main.schoolLabel: Thai Forest · Ajahn Chah line (Cittaviveka / Chithurst)
main.bio: Senior monk at Cittaviveka (Chithurst) in the Ajahn Chah tradition.

main.name: Ajahn Viradhammo
main.schoolLabel: Thai Forest · Ajahn Chah line (Tisarana, Canada)
main.bio: Latvian-Canadian monk ordained in Thailand under Ajahn Chah; founding abbot of Tisarana Buddhist Monastery in Ontario.

main.name: Ajahn Sona
main.schoolLabel: Thai Forest · Ajahn Chah line (Birken Forest, Canada)
main.bio: Canadian monk and co-founder of Birken Forest Monastery in British Columbia, in the Thai forest tradition; known for practical talks on jhāna and daily life.

main.name: Ajahn Anan
main.schoolLabel: Thai Forest · Ajahn Chah line (Wat Marp Jan)
main.bio: Thai monk who ordained under Ajahn Chah in 1975 and founded Wat Marp Jan in Rayong; teaches weekly in Thai with English translation.

main.name: Ajahn Kalyano
main.schoolLabel: Thai Forest · Ajahn Chah line via Ajahn Anan (Buddha Bodhivana)
main.bio: Australian monk, a long-time student and translator of Ajahn Anan; abbot of Buddha Bodhivana Monastery near Melbourne.

main.name: Ajahn Chandako
main.schoolLabel: Thai Forest · Ajahn Chah line (Vimutti, NZ)
main.bio: American-born monk of the Ajahn Chah tradition; abbot of Vimutti Buddhist Monastery in New Zealand.

main.name: Ajahn Jayasaro
main.schoolLabel: Thai Forest · Ajahn Chah line (Wat Pah Nanachat, Panyaprateep)
main.bio: English monk ordained by Ajahn Chah, former abbot of Wat Pah Nanachat; teaches mostly in Thai, with some English retreats and talks.

channels.name: ธรรมะ โดย พระอาจารย์ชยสาโร/ Dhamma by Ajahn Jayasaro

main.name: Thanissaro Bhikkhu
main.schoolLabel: Thai Forest · Dhammayut line of Ajaan Lee / Ajaan Fuang (Metta Forest)
main.bio: American monk of the Thai Dhammayut forest tradition, trained under Ajaan Fuang (a student of Ajaan Lee); abbot of Metta Forest Monastery and prolific translator of the Pāli Canon.

channels.name: Short Dhamma Talks by Thanissaro Bhikkhu

main.name: Sayadaw U Paṇḍita
main.bio: Burmese meditation master in the Mahasi Sayadaw lineage; abbot of Panditarama in Yangon and a major teacher of the first generation of Western insight teachers.

main.name: Sayadaw U Sīlānanda
main.bio: Burmese scholar-monk trained in the Mahasi tradition; founded the Theravada Buddhist Society of America and taught Abhidhamma and satipaṭṭhāna in California.

main.name: Sayadaw U Thuzana
main.bio: Burmese teacher in the Mahasi lineage who leads retreats at the Tathagata Meditation Center.

main.name: Sayadaw U Nandasiri
main.bio: Burmese teacher in the Mahasi lineage who leads retreats at the Tathagata Meditation Center.

main.name: S. N. Goenka
main.schoolLabel: Burmese · U Ba Khin / Goenka Vipassana
main.bio: Burmese-born Indian teacher of vipassanā in the lineage of Sayagyi U Ba Khin; founded the worldwide network of ten-day courses.

main.name: Sayadaw U Tejaniya
main.bio: Burmese teacher, student of the late Shwe Oo Min Sayadaw, known for a relaxed "natural awareness" approach to mindfulness in daily life.

main.name: Bhante Gunaratana
main.bio: Sri Lankan monk, founder of the Bhavana Society in West Virginia and author of "Mindfulness in Plain English".

channels.name: The Bhavana Society of West Virginia

main.name: Bhikkhu Anālayo
main.bio: German-born monk and scholar ordained in Sri Lanka; specialist in comparative study of the Pāli Nikāyas and Chinese Āgamas, and author of widely used books on satipaṭṭhāna.

main.name: Bhikkhu Bodhi
main.bio: American monk ordained in Sri Lanka, former president and editor of the Buddhist Publication Society; translator of the Majjhima, Saṃyutta and Aṅguttara Nikāyas and founder of Buddhist Global Relief.

main.name: Joseph Goldstein
main.bio: American insight meditation teacher, co-founder of the Insight Meditation Society; trained with Anagarika Munindra, Dipa Ma, S. N. Goenka and Sayadaw U Pandita.

main.name: Sharon Salzberg
main.bio: American teacher and co-founder of the Insight Meditation Society, best known for teaching mettā (loving-kindness).

main.name: Tara Brach
main.bio: American psychologist and insight meditation teacher, founder of the Insight Meditation Community of Washington.

main.name: Swami Sarvapriyananda
main.bio: Monk of the Ramakrishna Order and minister of the Vedanta Society of New York, known for clear lectures on Advaita Vedānta and consciousness.

channels.name: Vedanta Society of New York - Archives

main.name: Swami Pavitrananda
main.bio: Monk of the Ramakrishna Order who led the Vedanta Society of New York from 1951; heard here in archival recordings.

channels.name: Vedanta Society of New York - Archives

main.name: Swami Tathagatananda
main.bio: Monk of the Ramakrishna Order and long-time head of the Vedanta Society of New York; heard here in archival recordings.

channels.name: Vedanta Society of New York - Archives

main.name: Swami Sarvadevananda
main.bio: Monk of the Ramakrishna Order and head of the Vedanta Society of Southern California.

main.name: Swami Satyamayananda
main.bio: Monk of the Ramakrishna Order who lectures at Vedanta Society centres.

main.name: Swami Atmavidyananda
main.bio: Monk of the Ramakrishna Order at the Vedanta Society of Southern California.

main.name: Swami Vedarupananda
main.bio: Monk of the Ramakrishna Order at the Vedanta Society of Southern California.

main.name: Swami Mahayogananda
main.bio: Monk of the Ramakrishna Order at the Vedanta Society of Southern California.

main.name: Swami Dhyanayogananda
main.bio: Monk of the Ramakrishna Order at the Vedanta Society of Southern California.

main.name: Swami Medhananda (Ayon Maharaj)
main.bio: Monk of the Ramakrishna Order and philosopher (Ayon Maharaj), author of studies of Ramakrishna's and Vivekananda's philosophy.

main.name: Pravrajika Vrajaprana
main.bio: Nun of the Sarada Convent (Vedanta Society of Southern California) and author of books on Vedanta.

main.name: Pravrajika Krishnaprana
main.bio: Nun of the Sarada Convent, Vedanta Society of Southern California.

main.name: Swami Tyagananda
main.bio: Monk of the Ramakrishna Order, head of the Ramakrishna Vedanta Society of Boston and Hindu chaplain at Harvard and MIT.

main.name: Swami Chetanananda
main.bio: Monk of the Ramakrishna Order, minister of the Vedanta Society of St. Louis and author of histories of Ramakrishna's disciples.

main.name: Swami Shivarchanananda
main.bio: Monk of the Ramakrishna Order at the Vedanta Society of St. Louis.

main.name: Swami Ishatmananda
main.bio: Monk of the Ramakrishna Order and head of the Vivekananda Vedanta Society of Chicago.

main.name: Swami Chinmayananda
main.bio: Indian teacher who studied with Swami Sivananda and Swami Tapovan Maharaj and founded the Chinmaya Mission, popularising Vedānta lectures in English.

main.name: Swami Tejomayananda
main.bio: Disciple of Swami Chinmayananda and former head of the Chinmaya Mission worldwide.

main.name: Swami Swaroopananda (Chinmaya Mission)
main.bio: Disciple of Swami Chinmayananda and current global head of the Chinmaya Mission.

main.name: Swami Dayananda Saraswati
main.bio: Indian teacher of Advaita Vedānta, founder of the Arsha Vidya Gurukulam and teacher of many traditional Vedānta teachers.

main.name: Swamini Svatmavidyananda
main.bio: Traditional teacher of Vedānta in the line of Swami Dayananda Saraswati.

main.name: Swami Tattvavidananda
main.bio: Senior disciple of Swami Dayananda Saraswati teaching Vedānta and Sanskrit.

main.name: Swami Viditatmananda
main.bio: Senior disciple of Swami Dayananda Saraswati, long associated with the Arsha Vidya Gurukulam.

main.name: Swami Tadatmananda
main.bio: American-born disciple of Swami Dayananda Saraswati; founder of the Arsha Bodha Center in New Jersey.

main.name: Radhanath Swami
main.bio: American-born Gaudiya Vaishnava teacher in ISKCON, a disciple of A. C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupada, and author of "The Journey Home".

main.name: Swami Niranjanananda Saraswati
main.bio: Successor of Swami Satyananda Saraswati and long-time head of the Bihar School of Yoga in Munger.

main.name: Swami Swaroopananda (Sivananda)
main.schoolLabel: Yoga Vedanta · Sivananda Yoga Vedanta Centres
main.bio: Senior acharya of the Sivananda Yoga Vedanta Centres, a disciple of Swami Vishnudevananda.

main.name: Swami Sitaramananda
main.schoolLabel: Yoga Vedanta · Sivananda Yoga Vedanta Centres
main.bio: Acharya of the Sivananda Yoga Farm in California, a disciple of Swami Vishnudevananda.

main.name: Swami Paramananda (Sivananda)
main.schoolLabel: Yoga Vedanta · Sivananda Yoga Vedanta Centres
main.bio: Teacher of the Sivananda Yoga Vedanta Centres (not the Ramakrishna-order Swami Paramananda, 1884–1940).

main.name: Swami Shambhudevananda
main.schoolLabel: Yoga Vedanta · Sivananda Yoga Vedanta Centres
main.bio: Teacher of the Sivananda Yoga Vedanta Centres.

main.name: Swami Brahmananda (Sivananda)
main.schoolLabel: Yoga Vedanta · Sivananda Yoga Vedanta Centres
main.bio: Teacher of the Sivananda Yoga Vedanta Centres (not the Ramakrishna-order Swami Brahmananda).

main.name: Gavin Flood
main.bio: British scholar of Hinduism and comparative religion at Oxford; academic director of the Oxford Centre for Hindu Studies.

channels.name: HDS Center for the Study of World Religions

main.name: Edwin Bryant
main.bio: American scholar of Hinduism at Rutgers, translator of the Yoga Sūtras and the tenth book of the Bhāgavata Purāṇa.

more_voices.name: Ajahn Dtun
more_voices.schoolLabel: Thai Forest · Ajahn Chah line (ordained under Ajahn Chah; Wat Boonyawad)
more_voices.bio: Thai monk ordained at Wat Nong Pah Pong with Ajahn Chah as preceptor (1978); trained with Ajahn Piak and Ajahn Anan and founded Wat Boonyawad in Chonburi.

channels.name: วัดบุญญาวาส Watboonyawad - Official

more_voices.name: Richard Gombrich
more_voices.bio: British Indologist, Boden Professor of Sanskrit at Oxford (1976–2004) and founder of the Oxford Centre for Buddhist Studies; supervised a generation of Buddhist-studies doctorates.

more_voices.name: Alexander Wynne
more_voices.bio: British scholar of early Buddhism; Oxford DPhil under Richard Gombrich, author of "The Origin of Buddhist Meditation", and an editor of the Journal of the OCBS.

more_voices.name: Rupert Gethin
more_voices.bio: British scholar of the Nikāyas and Abhidhamma, emeritus professor at Bristol and president of the Pali Text Society; PhD at Manchester under Lance Cousins.

channels.name: The Ho Center for Buddhist Studies at Stanford

more_voices.name: Steven Collins
more_voices.bio: British scholar of Pāli Buddhism at Chicago, author of "Selfless Persons" and "Nirvana and Other Buddhist Felicities"; Oxford DPhil under Richard Gombrich.

channels.name: University of Chicago Center for Practical Wisdom

more_voices.name: Jeffery D. Long
more_voices.bio: American scholar of Hindu and Jain traditions at Elizabethtown College, closely associated with the Vedanta Societies.

more_voices.name: T. K. V. Desikachar
more_voices.bio: Son and student of T. Krishnamacharya; founded the Krishnamacharya Yoga Mandiram in Chennai and taught yoga adapted to the individual.

more_voices.name: Wendy Doniger
more_voices.bio: American Indologist at the University of Chicago, translator of Sanskrit texts and author of "The Hindus: An Alternative History".

more_voices.name: Nicholas Sutton
more_voices.bio: Scholar of the Mahābhārata and Bhagavad Gītā who teaches the OCHS online courses.

figures.name: Lance Cousins
figures.bio: British scholar of Pāli and Abhidhamma (Manchester, Oxford) and samatha meditation teacher; supervised Rupert Gethin.

figures.name: Paul Williams
figures.bio: British scholar of Mahāyāna Buddhism at Bristol; taught Alexander Wynne and introduced Steven Collins to Gombrich.

figures.name: Katukurunde Ñāṇananda
figures.bio: Sri Lankan forest monk and author of "Concept and Reality" and the "Nibbāna – The Mind Stilled" sermons.

figures.name: Balangoda Ānanda Maitreya
figures.bio: Sri Lankan scholar-monk who was Bhikkhu Bodhi's preceptor.

figures.name: Ajahn Piak
figures.bio: Thai disciple of Ajahn Chah and abbot of Wat Pah Cittabhavana; Ajahn Dtun and Ajahn Anan trained alongside him.

figures.name: Swami Tapovan Maharaj
figures.bio: Himalayan Vedānta master at Uttarkashi; Swami Chinmayananda's teacher.

figures.name: Swami Vishnudevananda
figures.bio: Disciple of Swami Sivananda who founded the Sivananda Yoga Vedanta Centres.

figures.name: Swami Satyananda Saraswati
figures.bio: Disciple of Swami Sivananda who founded the Bihar School of Yoga (1963).

figures.name: T. Krishnamacharya
figures.bio: South Indian yoga teacher whose students (Desikachar, Iyengar, Pattabhi Jois, Indra Devi) shaped modern postural yoga.

figures.name: B. K. S. Iyengar
figures.bio: Student and brother-in-law of Krishnamacharya; founder of Iyengar Yoga.

figures.name: K. Pattabhi Jois
figures.bio: Student of Krishnamacharya; founder of Ashtanga Vinyasa Yoga in Mysore.

figures.name: Chaitanya Mahāprabhu
figures.bio: Bengali saint whose ecstatic Krishna devotion founded the Gaudiya Vaishnava tradition.

figures.name: Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī
figures.bio: Founder of the Gaudiya Math and guru of A. C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupada.

figures.name: A. C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupāda
figures.bio: Founder of ISKCON (1966), who brought Gaudiya Vaishnavism to the West.

figures.name: Daniel H. H. Ingalls
figures.bio: Harvard Sanskritist; supervised Wendy Doniger's Harvard PhD.

figures.name: Swami Paramarthananda
figures.bio: Chennai-based disciple of Swami Dayananda, known for systematic English Vedānta classes (no official YouTube channel found).
